overview: ASCEND’s UAS work connects aircraft engineering with atmospheric research. Fixed-wing aircraft are intended to measure horizontal variability, while multirotor aircraft support detailed vertical profiles in the lower atmosphere.

Teams will integrate sensors and data systems, test their platforms, and evaluate measurements alongside balloon and surface observations. The aircraft resources below support the engineering skills needed for that work.

YELLOWSTONE will serve primarily as an onboard data logger on UAS and will also transmit data to a ground station. It shares its PCB with the balloon system, while using a UAS-specific firmware variant.

overview: ASCEND’s science plan connects measurements near the surface with observations higher in the atmosphere. Teams will investigate how smoke layers, atmospheric conditions, and terrain relate to air quality downwind.

The work includes sensor evaluation, comparison of surface and airborne observations, and analysis alongside NASA datasets. The aim is to understand both the atmosphere and the limits of the instruments used to measure it.

title: High-Altitude Ballooning
description: Use radiosondes and student-integrated balloon payloads to investigate atmospheric structure and the vertical distribution of smoke.

subsections.title: Scientific Investigations
subsections.description: Investigate vertical smoke layers, gaps in remote-sensing observations, and transport near the tropopause.

overview: Small meteorological balloons with radiosondes provide profiles of temperature, pressure, humidity, and wind. Larger high-altitude balloons support student-integrated payloads for particulate measurements and other observations through a deeper atmospheric column.
ASCEND plans to combine these observations with UAS and surface measurements. Shared sensing, data logging, and comparison practices will help teams connect observations across platforms.
Balloons will use YELLOWSTONE for tracking, flight termination, and data logging. The same PCB will also fly on UAS, with a separate HAB firmware variant for the balloon mission.
